Brother Blacksmith

Overview

Brother Blacksmith finds Zak after his escape through the caves and speaks for him before Khatul. He fled enslavement after his smithy burned down and maintains secret trade with city merchants to equip the Shelter. He asks Zak to settle an old grievance against the slavedriver brothers Lash-Aga and Whip-Aga, a request that brings him into conflict with Khatul’s caution. [1, 2, 3, 4]

Acceptance into the Last Shelter

Beyond the caves, Brother Blacksmith finds Zak and vouches for him before Brother Khatul. The brotherhood’s leader fears imperial spies and requires the Emperor’s Signet Ring, taken from a cyclops who killed its courier. Possessing such an object compromises the newcomer with the authorities and makes the test more than a feat of strength. After Zak returns, Khatul accepts him as Brother Blondie and offers the refuge as a new home. Zak explains his promise to find At-Zako and return to Gipath. Khatul respects that purpose and asks those who can help to support him; Brother Blind can teach him greater dexterity. [1, 5, 6]

Sahilia’s cache and the Joon collector

Sahilia supplies the next lead through her own theft. Antiquities she stole from Baluddin remain hidden near the city, and Zak recovers them to arrange a meeting. Khatul and Brother Blacksmith help choose the secluded trading place, keeping strangers away from the Shelter. Baluddin admits recognising At-Zako as a living Joon and wanting to keep him in his own house. Imperial scholars took the young man away. Later, Taivo summoned the collector to identify those scholars’ mutilated bodies. The missing youth’s trail now leads to the necromancers rather than a living prisoner whom Zak can simply rescue. [7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13]
